title: Statutory Requirement Policy
html:
A. Purpose: To provide guideline instruction for satisfying the statutory requirements and to provide a mechanism for updating the same as and when required.

B. Scope: Hospital wide.

C. Definitions:

  • Act is a statement of the law that governs a particular topic e.g. health. It begins as a Bill in Parliament and is approved as an Act by Parliament. It may be reprinted is significantly amended.
  • License is a formal permission from the proper authorities to perform certain acts or to carry on a certain business, which without such permission would be illegal.

D. Policy:

i. The management of the hospital will undertake the follow activities:

  • Satisfy all statutory requirements as required by the law of the land.
  • Preserve the required acts and licenses in a safe manner facilitating easy retrieval of same incase demanded by an appropriate authority or for internal reference.
  • Display the same for the perusal of the general public incase so required by law.
  • Keep a track of any amendment/changes in the prevailing law and update the same as per the law.
  • Ensure initiation of timely efforts for the renewal of licenses / registrations / certifications as and when needed.

ii. The hospital is government by the following statutory requirements:

  • License :
    • Building Permit (From the Municipality).
    • No objection certificate from the Chief Fire Officer.
    • Authorization from Maharashtra Pollution Control for Handling Biomedical Waste.
    • X-ray room layout approval from AERB.
    • Vehicle registration certificates.
    • License for the blood bank.
    • Authorization for MTP.

2. Acts:

  • Narcotics and Psychotropic substances Act.
  • Air (prevention and control of pollution) Act, 1981.
  • Biomedical waste management handling rules 1998.
  • Consumer protection Act, 1986.
  • Dentist regulations, 1976.
  • Drugs and cosmetics Act, 1940.
  • Employees provident fund Act, 1952.
  • Equal remuneration Act, 1976.
  • Fatal accidents Act, 1955.
  • Indian lunacy Act, 1912.
  • Indian medical council Act and code of medical ethics, 1956.
  • Indian nursing council Act, 1947.
  • Indian penal code, 1860.
  • Indian trade unions Act, 1926.
  • Maternity benefit Act, 1961.
  • MTP Act, 1971.
  • Minimum wages Act, 1948.
  • National building code.
  • Negotiable instruments Act, 1881.
  • Payment of wages Act, 1936.
  • Persons with disability Act, 1995.
  • Pharmacy Act, 1948.
  • PNDT Act, 1996.
  • Protection of human rights Act, 1993.
  • BARC, Act.
  • Registration of births and deaths Act, 1969.
  • Tax deducted at source Act.
  • Constitution of India.
  • Transplantation of human organs Act, 1994.

Custodian of Acts and Licenses:

  • All the acts will be stored centrally in the custody of the Administrator of the hospital.
  • Hospital staff members will have an access to the acts for any reference after obtaining permission from the Administrator.
  • A copy of the licenses will be stored by the individual department under the ambit of the license which will be displayed in the concerned department.
  • All original copy of the licenses will be stored centrally under the custody of the in charge clerk in the administrative department.
